extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, researchers, and technically-minded public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative comments about entries to the Royal Photographic Society exhibition, emphasizing what makes photographic exhibits of scientific/technical interest and quality. Also includes related submission and procedural requirements elsewhere on the page (e.g., essay contest rules, job application criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for series showing progressive changes
rubrics_metrics.description: There are still a good many single photographs of an animal, a flower, or an insect that have no particular interest, or if they have it is not indicated; but there are many series showing progressive changes, such as Dr. S. Hastings’s nine illustrations of soil formation in the Alps, in which he shows the bare rock covered at first with crustaceous lichens, and traces the stages of vegetation until an alpine meadow is produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibits that present a sequence or series documenting progressive change (processes, development, stages) are more valuable and informative than isolated single images; authors should provide context to indicate why images are of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical quality of photographic work
rubrics_metrics.description: With scarcely any exception the photography in this section is excellent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High technical standard (sharpness, exposure, composition appropriate to purpose) is expected for scientific/technical photographic exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing instrument performance (astronomical focus images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dr. J. S. Plaskett shows four photographs taken at the focus of the 72-inch reflecting telescope at the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory, Victoria, B.C., which also give evidence of the accuracy of figure of the mirror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs that demonstrate the performance or accuracy of scientific instruments (e.g., telescope mirror figure) are particularly valuable as evidence and should be presented to reveal instrument characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical spectroscopy and calibration plates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mount Wilson Observatory contributes specimens ... as well as photographs of the unusual spectra of seven stars, made with these instruments. Enlarged negative prints of a latitude variation plate and a wave-length plate are among the exhibits of the Astronomer Royal, Greenwich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectral plates and calibration prints (e.g., wavelength plates, latitude variation plates) that document observations and permit comparison are important contributions to scientific photographic exhibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of accurate comparative scales by photographic means
rubrics_metrics.description: The production of accurate comparative scales by photographic means is fully described and illustrated by Mr. A. E. Bawtree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographic methods that produce reliable comparative scales (for measurement or calibration) are of high scientific utility and should include clear description and illustration of technique and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forensic/documentary photographic methods to reveal alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Wilfred Mark Webb shows how, by chemical and photographic means, a Russian internal passport was made to yield deleted details which showed that the document had done duty on four separate occasions for as many different persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques that reveal deletions or tampering in documents (chemical/photographic processing) are valid scientific photographic contributions; describe methods and show recovered details to support findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photomicrography and plate grain studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful photomicrographs of silver bromide crystals, at 3000 diameters, by Mr. A. P. H. Trivelli, and the characteristic curves of modern high-speed dry plates with photomicrographs of the grains that constitute the sensitive material by Mr. J. W. Grundy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-magnification photomicrographs that reveal emulsion grain structure and relate to characteristic response curves are valuable; pair imagery with quantitative curves or measurements where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-altitude/condition-specific photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Grundy also contributes a fine series of photographs taken under various conditions from a height of about 14,000 feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographic series documenting performance under specific or extreme conditions (e.g., high altitude) are useful; include conditions and technical parameters to contextualize results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radiographic technique demonstration (Potter–Bucky diaphragm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Among numerous radiographs by several workers the effect of the Potter-Bucky diaphragm is shown by Mr. R. B. Wilsey. This diaphragm ... absorbs a large proportion of the scattered rays. It is placed between the patient and the film, and moved during the exposure so that it may not show on the radiograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radiographic exhibits that demonstrate the effect of technical apparatus or methods (e.g., grids/diaphragms reducing scatter) should show before-and-after or explanatory comparisons and describe device operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour transparency and autochrome reproduction fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a large collection of colour transparencies, and—among them some of scientific interest, but the most remarkable are the stereoscopic slides made on autochrome plates by Mr. S. Pegler. The successful reproduction of the colour and the brilliancy of silver plate, various articles of jewellery, and coloured stones, together with the realistic appearance, demonstrates possibilities of this method...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color transparency and autochrome entries should demonstrate accurate color reproduction, brilliancy, and realistic rendering of subjects; stereoscopic realism adds value for demonstrations of appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/industrial contributions on plate manufacture and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many exhibits that deal with the technicalities of gelatine plate manufacture and the statistical properties of plates by workers in America, as well as in this country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions that address manufacturing processes and statistical characterization of photographic materials (e.g., plate sensitivity, grain distribution) are important; include data and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle — indicate scientific interest of a single image
rubrics_metrics.description: There are still a good many single photographs ... that have no particular interest, or if they have it is not indicated ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If presenting single images, explicitly indicate their scientific relevance or interest (captioning, explanatory notes) to justify inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blackwell Prize Essay — submission and identification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The BLACKWELL PRIZE of THIRTY GUINEAS, Open to Unrestricted Competition, will be awarded in 1923 for the Best Essay on 'The Sculptured and Inscribed Stones of the North-east and North of Scotland.' Essays must be lodged with the Secretary of the UNIVERSITY on or before January 1, 1923. Each Essay must bear a Motto, and be accompanied by a Sealed Envelope bearing the same Motto, and enclosing the Name and Address of the writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural requirements exactly: submit by deadline, include a motto on the essay, and include a sealed envelope labelled with the same motto containing author identification; failure to comply may disqualify entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headmaster (Leeds Grammar School) applicant qualifications and application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold Honours Degrees of a University in the United Kingdom or the British Dominions. Salary £1200, rising ... House free of rent, rates, and external repairs provided. Duties to begin as from January 1, 1923. Applications, with references and 2 pies of not more than 3 recent testimonials, to be sent in so as to be received not later than October 31, 1922, to the CLERK TO THE GOVERNORS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should meet degree requirements, prepare references and concise testimonials, and submit complete applications by the stated deadline to the specified address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecturer in Physiological Department (University of Birmingham) application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council invites applications for the stipendiary post (£300 per annum). Applications, with testimonials, should be sent to the undersigned not later than October 16. No special form of application is required. The Candidate elected will be required to enter upon the duties at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit testimonials and application by deadline; no prescribed form—provide customary supporting documents and be prepared to begin duties immediately if appointed.
